title: Which of five apps should take a three-project limit on its free plan first in 2027, and what it adds to that app's 2027 revenue, with each app's recurring revenue bridge for the year to 30 September 2026
subdomain: churn-propensity-uplift-modeling (the response of free accounts a new plan limit stops, read from the accounts an existing limit already stops and set against unstopped accounts, sized as the limit's addition to an app's revenue)
prompt_shape: 03: one of five apps with its sized addition, and each app's recurring revenue bridge (twenty figures)
stated_inputs: the Plus price and the free-plan revenue per active free account for each app (free_plan_limit_paper_2027.pdf, section 4)

sources.origin: generated by task305/generator/make.py (seeded, deterministic) around a fictional UK software company with five apps on free and paid plans: every account's months from each app's launch (sign-up, projects, storage, use, upgrades and departures), a research panel of one account in twenty-five, the monthly count of free accounts by active projects, the billing platform's subscriptions and events for the paying accounts, and the finance team's policy and plan rates; every organisation, product and person is invented, and no real dataset is reproduced.
